name: WeakMethod.__new__
note: review: WM.new treats every object with __self__/__func__ as success, so the TypeError from ref.__new__(cls, obj, _cb) (:61) for a __self__ that cannot be weakly referenced (a bound method of a __slots__ class without __weakref__) and from ref(func, _cb) (:62) is missing, as is a non-AttributeError from meth.__self__ (:48); the new-conjuncts of WeakMethodBasics are rfl on the definition, and only WeakMethodCallbackOnce (the _cb closure, :53-60) pins anything.

name: WeakMethod.__eq__
note: review: ref.__eq__ is weakref_richcompare, which returns PyObject_RichCompare(obj, other_obj) (Objects/weakrefobject.c:269), an arbitrary object that may raise, and `x and y` (:79) returns that object when falsy; the model forces Bool through an infallible q, and the theorem only pins the dead branch (:77-78) and NotImplemented.

name: WeakMethod.__ne__
note: review: ref.__ne__ calls the referent's own __ne__ (weakref_richcompare with Py_NE), but WM.ne uses `!q`, the negated __eq__, so the proven `ne = map not eq` merges two methods CPython keeps separate and is false for a referent whose __ne__ is not the negation of its __eq__; raising or non-bool results are again not expressible.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__init__
note: review: WvdDeath pins the remove closure (:105-110) through onDeath, but the update call (:113) is unpinned: WvdInit only says init returns some ok dictionary with eager = true, which `init _ _ := .ok empty` also satisfies.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__getitem__
note: review: Keys are an abstract DecidableEq K, so `self.data[key]` (:116) cannot raise from the key's __hash__/__eq__ (wvd[[1]] raises TypeError: unhashable); the live/dead/missing branches are mirrored and pinned against items().

name: WeakValueDictionary.__delitem__
note: review: No unhashable or raising-key path (DecidableEq K); WvdWrites only says a missing key raises KeyError and the deleted key is no longer `in`, so a delitem that empties the whole dict also satisfies it.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__len__
note: review: `d.len = d.data.length` is rfl on a one-line definition; the body is `len(self.data)`, a trivial: exclusion, not coverage.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__contains__
note: review: contains returns a total Bool, but the try at :129-132 catches only KeyError: an unhashable key raises TypeError out of `in`, and a KeyError raised by the key's __hash__/__eq__ is swallowed into False; neither is expressible with DecidableEq K.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__repr__
note: review: The class name and address are inputs, and the conjunct is the definition restated (rfl); nothing is pinned.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__setitem__
note: review: KeyedRef(value, ...) then the dict store is mirrored and WvdWrites is a good get-after-set property, but the store cannot fail on the key (unhashable key, raising __eq__ on a collision), so the order \"TypeError for the value before the key is hashed\" is not expressible either.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__deepcopy__
note: review: deepcopy(key, memo) (:157) is an infallible `dc : K -> K`, self.__class__() (:153, unlike copy's WeakValueDictionary()) is not modelled, and WvdCopy assumes dc injective, an undocumented hypothesis that removes the case where two keys deep-copy to equal keys.

name: WeakValueDictionary.get
note: review: The three branches (:161-171) are mirrored and pinned against items(), but with DecidableEq K the lookup cannot raise: an unhashable key raises TypeError out of get even with a default, and a KeyError from the key's __hash__/__eq__ becomes the default via `except KeyError` (:163).

name: WeakValueDictionary.items
note: review: items is a generator that derefs each snapshot entry lazily (:174-177); the model returns an eager list in one World, so a value dying between next() calls (CPython skips it) and an insert before the first next() (CPython's snapshot sees it) are not expressible, and the .copy() snapshot has no effect in the model.

name: WeakValueDictionary.keys
note: review: Lazy generator over a snapshot (:180-182) modelled as an eager list in a fixed World, so deaths or writes during iteration cannot be stated; keys = map fst items is pinned only relative to items.

name: WeakValueDictionary.itervaluerefs
note: review: The snapshot is taken at the first next(), not at the call (:196), which the eager list cannot express; the only property is `itervaluerefs = valuerefs`, rfl between two identical definitions, which any function used for both satisfies.

name: WeakValueDictionary.values
note: review: Lazy generator over a snapshot (:199-202) modelled as an eager list in a fixed World; a death between yields is not expressible.

name: WeakValueDictionary.pop
note: review: `except KeyError` (:214) also swallows a KeyError from the key's __hash__/__eq__ and lets an unhashable TypeError through, neither expressible with DecidableEq K; WvdPopSetdefault only says the popped key is no longer `in` (a pop that clears the dict passes) and says nothing about data after a dead or missing pop.

name: WeakValueDictionary.setdefault
note: review: Branches (:225-233) are mirrored and the live/dead cases pinned, but the `except KeyError` lookup (:226-228) cannot fail on the key (unhashable TypeError, KeyError from __hash__ treated as missing).

name: WeakValueDictionary.update
note: review: `other` is a ready list, so hasattr(other, \"items\") (:238), dict(other) (:239, e.g. a non-iterable or a 3-tuple element) and other.items() (:240) cannot raise; WvdUpdate covers only all-object values through `update (some ...)`, so the dictFrom pairs branch and the partial update the docstring claims are unpinned.

name: WeakValueDictionary.valuerefs
note: review: The only statement is `itervaluerefs = valuerefs` (rfl); a valuerefs returning [] satisfies it, so nothing about the returned references (one per entry, in order, dead ones included) is pinned.

name: WeakValueDictionary.__ior__
note: review: `d.ior objs = d.update (some objs)` is an alias restated by rfl; the model also always passes `other` as items, skipping update's dict(other) branch for a non-Mapping iterable (:238-239), and never states that self is returned.

name: KeyedRef.__new__
note: review: KRef.new drops the callback argument of ref.__new__(type, ob, callback) (:290), and WvdInit's KRef conjuncts are rfl on a one-line definition; WvdDeath never unfolds KRef.new.

name: KeyedRef.__init__
note: review: No Lean function mirrors it (the model only says it \"adds nothing\") and no theorem unfolds it; it only forwards (ob, callback) to ref.__init__, so it should be an excluded no-behaviour row, not modelled.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__delitem__
note: review: Eqv is a total Bool and hashing is not modelled, so an unhashable weakrefable key (a class with __eq__ and no __hash__) or a raising __eq__ cannot be expressed; no theorem states a successful delete, so a delitem that always raises KeyError after ref() satisfies WkdPopSetdefault and WkdNonWeak.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__getitem__
note: review: hash(ref(key)) calls hash(key) (:326), so a weakrefable unhashable key raises TypeError; the model has no hash and WkdReads says such a key gives KeyError or a value, which is false about CPython; __eq__ raising or re-entering is also not expressible.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__len__
note: review: `len(self.data)`: WkdReads only proves `keyrefs.length = len`, both `data.length` by definition (rfl); a trivial: exclusion, not coverage.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__repr__
note: review: The class name and address are inputs and the conjunct restates the definition (rfl).

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__setitem__
note: review: setRef mirrors \"an equal key keeps its ref\" and WkdWrites is a good property, but the store cannot fail or re-enter (no hash, total Bool __eq__): an unhashable weakrefable key raises TypeError in CPython and a value in the model.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__deepcopy__
note: review: deepcopy(value, memo) (:353) is an infallible `dc`, though deep-copying a value often raises (a lock, a generator), memo and self.__class__() (:349) are not modelled, and the theorem cannot see that memo never maps id(self) to new (see the suspected defect).

name: WeakKeyDictionary.get
note: review: `self.data.get(ref(key), default)` (:357) raises TypeError for a weakrefable unhashable key even with a default; the model returns the default.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__contains__
note: review: Only ref()'s TypeError is caught (:360-363); `wr in self.data` (:364) raises TypeError for a weakrefable unhashable key (and whatever __eq__ raises), but contains is a total Bool.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.items
note: review: Lazy generator over a snapshot (:367-370) modelled as an eager list in a fixed World; a key dying between next() calls is not expressible.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.keys
note: review: Lazy generator (:373-376) modelled as an eager list in a fixed World.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.values
note: review: Lazy generator (:381-383) modelled as an eager list in a fixed World.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.keyrefs
note: review: The only statement is `keyrefs.length = len`; any list of the right length (e.g. one ref repeated) satisfies it, so the refs and their order are unpinned.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.pop
note: review: The model takes the first of any number of defaults, but `self.data.pop(ref(key), *args)` (:405) is dict.pop, which raises TypeError for two or more defaults (the model copies WeakValueDictionary.pop's args[0]); WkdPopSetdefault never says the found entry is removed, so a pop that leaves it passes; the unhashable path is missing too.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.setdefault
note: review: Mirrored and pinned (an existing value is kept, otherwise the default is stored), but dict.setdefault on ref(key, ...) cannot fail on hashing or __eq__ in the model.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.update
note: review: The 3.15.2 keyword refusal first (:411-414) is mirrored and stated, but hasattr/type({})(dict)/dict.items() (:417-419) are infallible over a list; dictOf (the pairs branch) is unpinned (WkdInit's conjunct restates updatePairs by rfl); the partial update after a non-weakrefable key is not stated; WkdOr's docstring still says the TypeError comes \"after dict has been applied\", the 3.14 order.

name: WeakKeyDictionary.__ior__
note: review: `ior = update (some objs)` is an alias restated by rfl, and the model passes `other` as items, skipping update's dict() branch for a non-Mapping iterable.

name: finalize.__init__
note: review: FinalizeInit pins presence, dirty, the counter and the failure path, but not the stored _Info: an init that stores another func or obj, atexit := false (contradicting \"By default atexit is true\") or a wrong index satisfies it, and no other theorem starts from init.

name: finalize.atexit
note: review: The getter: FinalizeOnce only states the registered case (`atexit = info.atexit`); the dead branch `bool(info)` giving False (:519) is unpinned, so a getter returning True for a dead finalizer passes, despite the docstring's claim.

name: finalize.atexit
note: review: The setter takes a Lean Bool, so bool(value) (:525) on an arbitrary object, including a raising __bool__, is not modelled; only set-then-get on the same live finalizer is stated, with no no-op for a dead one and no frame for the others.

name: finalize.__repr__
note: review: type(self).__name__ (:531, :534) is hard-coded \"finalize\" (a subclass shows its own name) and %r of the object's type name is rendered as '{tn}'; the theorem restates the two format strings, leaving the registered-but-dead branch unstated.

name: finalize._exitfunc
note: review: gc.disable/enable (:551-554, :575-576), observable through gc.isenabled() in a finalizer, is not modelled, and onHook cannot raise; ExitfuncOrder assumes PlainRun (no func raises or creates a finalizer), which removes the excepthook path, the BaseException abort and the dirty re-select (:557-570), and also assumes dirty = false, though __init__ always leaves _dirty True.
